name: Push-up
notes: body in straight line from head to heels
why: You push the floor away until the arms are straight, then lower with the whole body in one line. The elbows stay near the ribs so the chest and triceps share the work.

name: Scapular Push-up
tempo_suggestion: 1 sec protract, 1 sec pause, 2 sec retract
notes: elbows stay locked; only the shoulder blades move
push the floor away to spread the shoulder blades apart
let the chest sink between the shoulder blades without the lower back sagging
why: The arms stay straight. You let the shoulder blades spread, then pull them forward around the ribs. It is a small motion that teaches the shoulder to sit on the ribcage.

name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Dumbbell Press
contraindications: rotator cuff tear or recent shoulder surgery
limited overhead shoulder mobility (lower back arches to compensate)
notes: squeeze the glute of the down knee to keep the ribs stacked over the pelvis
press slightly in front of the head, finishing with the biceps near the ear
don't lean away from the working arm
why: One knee is down and the other foot is forward. You press one dumbbell overhead without leaning, then switch arms.

name: Face Pull
progression_path: Face Pull with External Rotation Hold
tempo_suggestion: 1 sec pull, 2 sec hold, 2 sec return
notes: set the anchor at upper-chest to eye height and use a rope or band
pull toward the face, splitting the rope and finishing with knuckles pointing back (external rotation)
keep ribs down; don't lean back to move more weight
why: You pull toward your face and finish with the hands apart and the knuckles back. The rear shoulder and upper back do the work.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
tempo_suggestion: 1 sec up, 1 sec pause, 2 sec down
notes: brace with a flat back; hand and knee on the bench
drive the elbow toward the hip, not straight up to the ear
avoid twisting the torso to finish the rep
why: One hand braces. You row the dumbbell toward the hip, then lower it without shrugging. Finish that arm, then switch.

name: Pull-up
notes: start each rep from a full hang with shoulders engaged (pulled slightly down)
chin clears the bar without craning the neck
avoid kipping; keep legs quiet and ribs down
why: From a hang, you pull until the chin clears the bar. If a full pull is not there yet, lower yourself slowly through the same path.

name: Glute Bridge
tempo_suggestion: 1 sec up, 2 sec hold, 2 sec down
contraindications: acute low back pain that worsens with extension
notes: drive through the heels; feet about hip-width, shins near vertical at the top
finish with hips extended by the glutes, not by arching the lower back
keep ribs down and pelvis slightly tucked at the top
why: Feet planted, you lift the hips until the body is a line from knee to shoulder. The glutes finish the lift. The low back does not arch to get higher.

name: Dumbbell Swing
tempo_suggestion: explosive hip snap; let the bell float, then hinge as it falls
contraindications: acute low back pain or disc herniation
unable to hip-hinge with a neutral spine
shoulder instability (bell pulls on the arms)
notes: one dumbbell held by the head
hip hinge, swing to chest height
Needs new art. Currently using the kettlebell swing image.
why: One dumbbell hangs between the legs. You hinge, then snap the hips so the bell floats up to chest height. The arms guide it. They do not lift it.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
contraindications: ankle sprain on the stance leg
notes: reps are per side; hold the dumbbell in the hand opposite the stance leg
keep hips square to the floor; don't let the raised hip open up
soft stance knee; lower until a hamstring stretch, spine stays neutral
why: You hinge on one leg and reach toward the floor with a long back. The standing hip stays square. Then the other leg.

name: Spanish Squat
tempo_suggestion: hold 30-45 sec at the working depth
contraindications: knee pain that increases during the hold (reduce depth)
notes: loop a heavy band behind both knees and anchor it to a sturdy post at knee height
sit back into the band so shins stay vertical and the knees don't drift forward
commonly used to load the quads/patellar tendon with less knee pain
why: A band holds you back at the knees so you can sit into a squat and stay. The quads work while the knees stay over the feet.

name: Goblet Squat
tempo_suggestion: 3 sec down, 1 sec pause, 1 sec up
contraindications: acute hip pain or hip impingement at depth (reduce depth)
notes: hold the weight at the chest with elbows pointing down
knees track over the toes; sit between the heels
keep the chest tall and heels down
why: One dumbbell sits at the chest while you sit between the hips. Elbows stay inside the knees. You stand by pushing the floor away.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
contraindications: hip flexor strain on the rear leg
notes: reps are per side; rear foot laces-down on the bench
front foot far enough forward that the heel stays down
slight forward torso lean shifts work to the glutes; upright shifts it to the quads
why: The back foot rests on a bench. You lower the back knee, then stand on the front leg. Finish that side, then switch.

name: Farmer's Carry
notes: stand tall, shoulders down and back, weights at the sides
walk heel-to-toe without the weights swinging
set the weights down with a hinge, not a rounded back
why: A weight in each hand. You walk tall, ribs down, without leaning. The hands and the trunk hold while the legs walk.

name: Suitcase Carry
tempo_suggestion: steady walk; time is per side
notes: don't lean toward or away from the weight; shoulders stay level
the side opposite the weight is doing the most work
why: One weight in one hand. You walk without leaning toward it or away from it. Then the other hand.

name: Waiter's Carry
tempo_suggestion: slow walk; time is per side
contraindications: limited overhead shoulder mobility (lower back arches to compensate)
notes: lock the elbow with biceps by the ear, wrist straight
ribs down; don't arch the lower back to get the weight overhead
start light: this is a stability drill
why: One weight stays overhead while you walk, ribs quiet. Then the other arm.

name: Pallof Press
tempo_suggestion: press out 1 sec, hold 2-3 sec, return 1 sec
contraindications: acute low back pain that worsens with bracing
notes: anti-rotation: the goal is to resist the cable, not to twist
stand side-on to the anchor, hands at the sternum, press straight out
why: A band or cable tries to turn you. You press the hands straight out and hold the trunk still. Then the other side.

name: Bird Dog
tempo_suggestion: reach 2 sec, hold 3-5 sec, return 2 sec
contraindications: knee pain when kneeling (use a pad)
notes: reps are per side; extend the opposite arm and leg
keep the hips level; imagine a cup of water on the lower back
reach long, not high; don't arch the lower back
why: From hands and knees you reach one arm and the opposite leg, then come back without rocking. Then the other pair.

name: Dumbbell Woodchop
contraindications: acute low back pain or disc herniation (loaded rotation)
notes: high-to-low diagonal chop across the body
Needs new art. Currently using the cable woodchop image.
why: Both hands hold one dumbbell. You lift it high and chop down across the body, turning from the hips. Then the other direction.

name: March in Place
why: A warm muscle stretches further and more safely.

name: Jumping Jacks
why: A warm muscle stretches further and more safely.

name: Leg Swings
why: You swing one leg forward and back, loose and easy, to wake the hip up. Then the other leg.
setup: Hold a chair or wall. Swing one leg forward and back.

name: Bodyweight Good Morning
why: Hands at the head or crossed, you hinge at the hips with a long back and stand back up. The hamstrings and glutes do the work.

name: Lunge 90 Hip Flexor
notes: press the top of your back foot down
setup: Kneeling lunge, front knee over ankle, hips over back knee, hips facing forward. Pad under the back knee.
common_mistake: Arching your low back instead of tucking.
why: A kneeling lunge opens the front of the back hip. You tuck the tail and stay, instead of arching the low back to feel more.

name: Lunge 90 Ankle Grab
notes: bring your foot to your butt, not your butt to your foot
setup: Same lunge. Bend your back knee and hold your shin or ankle, or use a strap.
common_mistake: Twisting your torso to reach the foot.
why: From the same lunge you bend the back knee and hold the ankle, so the front of the thigh joins the hip flexor stretch.

name: Half Split Hip Flexor
notes: let gravity pull your hips down
setup: Walk your front foot forward about 6 inches and sink your hips low. Front knee over ankle. Blocks under your hands.
common_mistake: Leaning forward over your front leg.
why: The back leg is straight behind you and the hips stay square. You sink a little and breathe, without dropping into the low back.

name: Half Split PNF
setup: Same position as the half split.
common_mistake: Holding your breath during the press.
why: Contract-relax lets your nervous system allow more range.

name: Half Split Ankle Grab
notes: tailbone points down toward your back knee
setup: From the half split, hold your back foot. A strap is fine.
why: In the half split you reach back for the ankle so the front of the thigh stretches with the hip.

name: Half Split Knee Taps
notes: the knee just grazes the mat
all the movement comes from your back leg
setup: Tuck your back toes and lift your back knee so the leg is straight.
common_mistake: Pushing your hips up with your front leg. It's fine to lean onto blocks.
why: From the half split you tap the back knee down and lift it again. The hip learns to bend and open without a long hold.

name: Hamstring Stretch Flexed
notes: lift your tailbone toward the wall behind you
setup: Rock your hips back over your back knee. Front leg straight, toes up.
common_mistake: Rounding your back to reach the foot.
why: One leg is straight in front, toes pulled toward you. You fold from the hip over that leg, back long.

name: Hamstring Stretch Pointed
notes: you may sink a little deeper
setup: Same as the flexed hamstring stretch, with your foot pointed.
why: The same fold, with the toes pointed, so the stretch sits higher in the hamstring and less in the calf.

name: Pyramid Pose
notes: hands on your thigh or blocks
setup: Stand in a short split stance with both legs straight and both hip bones facing forward.
common_mistake: Your back hip opening out to the side.
why: The front leg is straight, the back heel is down, and you fold over the front leg from the hip.

name: Pyramid Good Morning
notes: hinge down with a flat back
press your front foot down to stand up
squeeze your glutes at the top
common_mistake: Rushing the reps or rounding your back.
why: From the pyramid stance you hinge up and down with a long back, so the hamstring stretch becomes a small strength move.

name: Front Split Hold
notes: hips square, pull your back hip forward
setup: Slide into your deepest comfortable front split. Blocks under your hands. A cushion under your hips if you need it.
common_mistake: Hips turning open to the side. You can let them open only after the minute is up.
why: You ease toward the split, front heel down and back knee or toes down, and breathe there. You do not force the hips to the floor.

name: Warm-up
notes: start slow before the first stretch
setup: Move easily for a few minutes. Get warm, not tired.
why: A warm muscle stretches further and more safely.

name: 45-Degree Back Extension
notes: evidence: RCTs: back-extensor strengthening reduces kyphosis angle (Bansal 2014 review; Sinaki long-term). Strongest kyphosis evidence.

name: Prone Cobra (Brügger)
notes: evidence: Common in meta-analysed UCS programs (Sepehri 2024 MA).

name: Serratus Wall Slide (Foam Roller)
notes: posture issue: rounded shoulders / scapular winging
evidence: SA + lower-trap activation core of UCS protocols; differs from wall angel (forearms on roller, protraction focus).

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
notes: posture issue: weak glutes / knee valgus
evidence: Highest glute-med EMG of rehab exercises (Distefano 2009).

name: Lateral Step-Down
notes: evidence: High glute-med EMG (Distefano 2009); used in valgus programs.

name: Banded Clamshell
notes: posture issue: weak glutes / knee valgus
evidence: Moderate-high glute-med EMG, valgus programs.

name: 90/90 Hip Lift with Balloon Breathing
notes: posture issue: rib flare / anterior pelvic tilt
evidence: PRI technique (Boyle 2010 clinical commentary); repositions ribs/pelvis.

name: Crocodile Breathing
notes: evidence: Breathing/rib-position drill; Bowman alignment emphasis (no direct trial cited).
overlap flag: partial overlap: diaphragm target

name: Heel Slide with TVA Brace
notes: posture issue: deep core / lumbar control
evidence: Motor-control core training evidence (Saragiotto 2016 Cochrane review).

name: Side-Lying Open Book
notes: posture issue: thoracic stiffness / rounded shoulders
evidence: Thoracic mobility component of UCS programs.

name: Band Shoulder Pass-Through
notes: evidence: Pec/anterior shoulder flexibility; stretching + strength best for UCS (2020 SR).

name: Prone Press-Up (McKenzie)
notes: evidence: McKenzie extension evidence for back pain (Lam 2018 MA).

name: Hip Airplane
notes: posture issue: weak glutes / knee valgus
evidence: Single-leg hip control used in valgus/glute programs (expert PT consensus; no direct trial cited).

name: Toe Yoga
notes: evidence: Intrinsic foot training improves arch (Mulligan 2013 trial); Bowman foot work.
overlap flag: near-dup risk: short-foot (prior list)

name: Kneeling Bench Lat & T-Spine Stretch
notes: evidence: Lat tightness limits overhead/thoracic extension; NASM CES inhibit-lengthen.

name: Reverse Hyperextension
notes: posture issue: weak glutes / anterior pelvic tilt
evidence: High glute activity without spinal load; NASM activation.

name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
notes: evidence: Stretching + strengthening reduces FHP (Sepehri 2024 MA).

name: Dumbbell Pullover Breathing (Rib Down)
notes: evidence: PRI rib-position concept; lower evidence.

name: Prone Lower-Trap Lift-Off (I-raise)
notes: evidence: Lower-trap EMG leader; in SA/LT protocols.
overlap flag: overlap: y-t-w-raise (use as regression)

name: Seated Leg Curl
notes: evidence: Maeo 2021: seated > lying leg curl for hamstring growth (lengthened).

name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
notes: evidence: Maeo 2023: overhead ~1.4-1.5x triceps growth vs pushdown.

name: Preacher Curl
notes: evidence: Pedrosa 2022: lengthened preacher partials grow distal biceps.

name: Barbell Back Squat
notes: evidence: Deep squats > partial for glutes/adductors (Kubo 2019).

name: Leg Press (Deep)
notes: evidence: Full ROM growth; low fatigue (Schoenfeld 2020 ROM review).

name: Leg Extension
notes: evidence: Only machine that isolates the quads incl. rectus femoris; reclined seat likely biases RF (mechanistic).

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
notes: evidence: Clavicular pec emphasis (Chaves 2020 EMG; Nippard).

name: Barbell Bench Press
notes: evidence: Gold-standard loaded press for chest/triceps.

name: Lat Pulldown
notes: evidence: High lat EMG across grips, scalable load (Lusk 2010).

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
notes: evidence: Removes lower-back limiter -> more upper-back stimulus (SBS/Nippard).

name: Dumbbell Fly (Deep Stretch)
notes: evidence: Stretch-loaded pec isolation; stretch-mediated hypertrophy.

name: Sissy Squat (Calisthenics)
notes: evidence: Bodyweight lengthened RF loading (calisthenics alt to leg extension); mechanistic.

name: Reverse Pec Deck / Rear Delt Fly
notes: evidence: Rear-delt gap; high EMG isolation.

name: Hammer Curl
notes: evidence: Neutral grip shifts load to brachialis/brachioradialis.

name: Seated Calf Raise
notes: evidence: Soleus focus; stretch pauses (Kassiano 2023: long-length calf training).

name: Dumbbell Pullover
notes: evidence: Lengthened lat/pec loading; EMG mixed.

name: Cable Crunch
notes: evidence: Loadable spinal flexion for abs hypertrophy.
